label: EU(7)-PIM: meprobamate
title: Meprobamate in an older person
statement: Meprobamate is on the list of medicines to avoid in older people because of the risk of drowsiness and confusion. If it must be used, the list advises a lower dose and longer gaps between doses when the kidneys work less well.

source.document: Renom-Guiteras A, Meyer G, Thurmann PA. The EU(7)-PIM list. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2015;71:861-875; ESM1 full list (row text from the official ESM1 DOCX parse saved 8 Nov 2026; legend from a hosted copy of the complete list)

plain_summary: Meprobamate, an old calming medicine, can cause drowsiness and confusion in people aged 65 or over.

medicine_groups.name: Meprobamate
medicine_groups.note: No Australian brand is listed. The history shows the ingredient name.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when the person is aged 65 or over and meprobamate is supplied, even once. If age is missing and meprobamate is supplied, report only a possible finding and ask whether the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: The record may omit why treatment began and whether it was supplied by another service or from overseas. Kidney function is unknown unless a dated result is recorded. Dispensing does not confirm how much is taken.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether meprobamate is still needed and whether a safer choice for anxiety or sleep is possible.
